_comment_DEP_002: RESOLVED: the PUBLISHED utils@0.1.0-alpha.1 declares "@hollis-studio/contracts": "*", which resolves off the `latest` dist-tag — for months that was 0.2.0-alpha.54, so anyone installing the published tarball got a second, months-old nested copy of contracts beside their own exact pin. Decision: mirror auth-client's DEP_001 resolution exactly — contracts is a PEER dependency (plus a devDependency for local build/typecheck), because unitConversions.ts imports the runtime value UNIT_CONVERSION from contracts and a normal dependency lets npm nest a second copy. Floor 0.2.0-alpha.85 is the oldest contracts version any current utils consumer installs (hollis-health-app root/server/web-admin/web-public; hollis-workouts is on alpha.89); ceiling <0.3.0 because UNIT_CONVERSION lives in the 0.2.x contract. No zod peer: utils does not import zod. Reviewed: 2026-09-20
name: @hollis-studio/utils
_comment_VERSION_001: Jumps 0.1.0-alpha.1 -> .4, skipping .2 and .3 on purpose: git tags utils-v0.1.0-alpha.2 and utils-v0.1.0-alpha.3 already exist on origin from the pre-workflow tagging era and were never published (the registry has only 0.1.0-alpha.1). .github/workflows/publish.yml triggers on a tag PUSH, so reusing either number would leave a release that can never be published by tag. alpha.4 is the first free number. Same trap applies to design-tokens: design-tokens-v0.2.0-alpha.2 is taken, so its next release must be 0.2.0-alpha.3 or later.
